column2: A company seeks SEHK participantship to run a cash equity brokerage. Which SFC licence must it hold?
column7: SEHK requires the applicant to be licensed for Type 1. Advice and portfolio management are different regulated activities.

column2: Which legal form qualifies a firm to apply for SEHK participantship in its own name?
column3: Hong Kong company limited by shares
column5: Overseas company with a local branch
column7: SEHK requires local incorporation as a company limited by shares. Registering a branch or a business name does not meet that condition.

column2: A licensed broker buys shares in HKEX. Which separate entitlement still forms part of its SEHK admission requirements?
column5: Right to a dividend from SEHK
column7: Holding shares gives an interest in the listed group. A firm seeking admission to the exchange must hold at least one trading right.

column2: A broker will route its own SEHK trades to an external clearer. Which contract meets the admission condition?
column3: CCASS agreement with a General Clearing Participant
column4: Custody agreement with an Investor Participant
column5: Agency agreement with a Direct Clearing Participant
column6: Settlement mandate with its designated bank
column7: An exchange participant can arrange third-party clearing through a binding clearing agreement with a General Clearing Participant. A banking or custody mandate serves a different purpose.

column2: Who must be among the responsible officers registered with SEHK by a cash market participant?
column6: The chair of the audit committee
column7: SEHK requires at least one executive director registered as a responsible officer at all times.

column2: An Options Broker Exchange Participant receives an order for a stock option. How does it reach HKATS?
column3: Through an Options Trading Exchange Participant
column4: Directly under its own broker participantship
column6: Through an OTC Clear clearing member
column7: Only an Options Trading Exchange Participant can enter these orders directly. The broker category must use such a participant.

column2: A broker combines a client's order for 800 shares with its own for 400. Just 900 fill. What allocation follows?
column7: A partial fill of a combined order goes to meet the client's instruction before the firm's. Here 100 shares remain after the client receives 800.

column2: Which employee is an analyst under the SFC rules on investment research?
column3: Author of securities reports distributed to clients
column4: Dealer giving comments incidental to execution
column5: Researcher preparing internal desk notes only
column6: Adviser giving a personal recommendation in private
column7: The definition covers people who prepare or publish investment research. It excludes each of the three narrower activities described.

column2: An analyst owns shares in an issuer she covers. Where must investors see disclosure of that holding?
column3: In the report covering the issuer
column5: In a notice to the issuer alone
column7: The analyst's financial interest belongs in the published research. An internal record cannot provide that disclosure to readers.

column2: Investment bankers want to check facts in an analyst's draft before publication. Who must oversee that review?
column7: The SFC permits investment banking to check factual accuracy under legal or compliance oversight. It does not grant the bankers authority to approve the recommendation.

column2: Which proposed pay component creates the specific link prohibited for a research analyst?
column3: Commission on closing a named underwriting deal
column4: Fixed salary for covering the banking sector
column5: Bonus based on the quality of published research
column7: The firm must not tie analyst compensation directly to a particular investment banking transaction. The concern is the financial stake in that deal.

column2: A policy-defined exceptional circumstance arises two business days after an analyst publishes research. Who can pre-approve a personal trade?
column3: The firm's legal or compliance function
column4: The firm's head of equity sales
column7: The normal restriction extends three business days after publication. A policy-defined exception requires prior approval from the relevant legal or compliance function.

column2: A fund holds bonds through an independent custodian. Who makes portfolio selections under its investment mandate?
column7: The manager implements the investment strategy for investors. The custodian's responsibility for the assets is separate from security selection.

column2: How should an authorised fund's trustee hold scheme assets relative to its own investments?
column3: Separately from the trustee's general estate
column4: In its house portfolio with an offsetting provision
column5: In a pool accessible to its general creditors
column6: In its trading account pending each valuation
column7: The trustee or custodian maintains separation between fund property and its own assets. This protects the fund when the service provider incurs liabilities.

column2: A firm can buy and sell securities for a client without seeking approval for each trade. Which activity describes its mandate?
column7: Properly delegated investment discretion is central to securities portfolio management. An adviser whose client makes each decision performs a different function.

column2: A multi-family office recommends listed securities for a fee. Clients make each decision and place their own orders. Which licence fits this service?
column7: The office is paid to advise on investments. The facts give it neither authority to manage portfolios nor responsibility for execution.

column2: A family trustee manages its trust property through an internal office. Why can this arrangement fall outside asset management licensing?
column3: The unit serves its trustee internally
column5: The office holds assets through nominees
column6: The portfolio contains only listed securities
column7: The trustee's own unit does not supply asset management to a third party. The SFC gives this structure as an example of an internal family arrangement.

column2: Two separately run single-family offices use the same premises and reception staff. What does this alone establish for licensing?
column3: Shared facilities without an automatic licensing obligation
column4: A regulated multi-family asset management business
column5: An exemption covering both offices' investment services
column6: A requirement to hold a joint securities dealing licence
column7: Shared administration alone does not determine licensing. The actual activities and the business carried on by each office matter.

column2: Which service provider maintains a listed issuer's Hong Kong register of holders on its behalf?
column7: The issuer appoints an approved securities registrar to maintain its register. A custodian can instead keep records for a particular client.

column2: Where can a client verify the current regulated activities of an individual who offers investment advice?
column3: SFC register of licensed persons and registered institutions
column4: HKEX directory of securities market makers
column5: HKMA register of authorised banking institutions
column6: SEHK list of trading and clearing participants
column7: The SFC register records the particulars of a person's licence or registration. Directories of firms with market access serve a different purpose.

column2: A client has HK$7.6 million in qualifying portfolio assets. How much more meets the individual professional investor portfolio threshold?
column7: The individual threshold is HK$8 million. The difference from HK$7.6 million is HK$0.4 million.

column2: An individual still qualifies as a professional investor and has unsettled trades. What is her earliest opportunity to revoke consent to that treatment?
column3: Before settlement and before the annual review
column4: After settlement but before the annual review
column5: Before settlement but after the annual review
column6: After settlement and after the annual review
column7: The right to revoke is available at any time. Neither pending trades nor the date of an annual review makes the person wait.

column2: A bank produces borrower credit scores for its own lending. Which service raises a Type 10 licensing question?
column3: Selling subscriptions to its issuer ratings
column4: Sending a private assessment to its sole commissioning client
column6: Circulating its lending limits to branch managers
column7: Providing ratings for subscribers is a credit rating service. A rating commissioned for the recipient's exclusive use, with no intended or expected wider distribution, is treated differently.

column2: Which outcome-linked rating fee is excluded from the contingent fee definition in paragraph 31 of the SFC rating code?
column3: Fee established by a court order
column4: Fee established by a trustee agreement
column5: Fee established by a board resolution
column6: Fee established by an issuer mandate
column7: The Code exempts fees set by a court or other public authority. A document approved by the agency, issuer or trustee does not establish that exemption.

column2: A rating agency earns 6% of its total annual revenue from one issuer, including its affiliates. What disclosure is required?
column4: Individual salaries of the rating team
column5: Value of the issuer's bond collateral
column6: Credit limits assigned by the issuer's banks
column7: The SFC threshold for naming the party or parties supplying the revenue is 5%. The rule addresses a possible dependence on that source.

column2: An ETF basket costs HK$100 per unit equivalent while its units sell for HK$102. Ignoring costs, which trade captures the premium?
column3: Buy the basket, create units and sell them
column4: Buy units, redeem them and sell the basket
column5: Sell the basket and buy units to hold
column6: Sell units, buy them back at the same price
column7: An authorised participant can exchange the basket for units. Selling them for more than the basket cost captures the gap before expenses.

column2: A dealer regularly posts both buying and selling prices for an ETF. What role is it performing?
column7: The market maker supplies two-sided quotes for investors trading on exchange. Creating units for the fund is a separate role a firm may also hold.

column2: Which organisation processes the exercise of a listed call on shares in a single Hong Kong company?
column7: Stock options traded on SEHK clear through SEOCH. HKSCC handles cash market clearing while HKCC clears futures exchange contracts.

column2: A dealer clears an exchange-traded Hang Seng Index futures position. Which group company takes the clearing role?
column7: HKFE provides the trading market. Its futures and options contracts clear through HKCC.

column2: A bank submits an eligible bilateral interest rate swap for central clearing in Hong Kong. Which HKEX subsidiary serves that market?
column7: The group's OTC clearing house serves eligible off-exchange interest rate and foreign exchange derivatives.

column2: Which HKEX group exchange operates the Ring for open-outcry trading in base metals?
column7: HKEX owns the London Metal Exchange, whose Ring is a venue for price discovery. LME Clear provides clearing services.

column2: Who handles day-to-day supervision of the securities business of a Hong Kong bank registered with the SFC?
column7: The HKMA is frontline supervisor for registered banks. The SFC retains overall responsibility for securities market regulation.

column2: A share closed at HK$20. What is the upper at-auction limit price during normal pre-opening order input?
column7: The initial limit is 15% above or below the previous close. Multiplying HK$20 by 1.15 gives HK$23.

column2: At 9:17 a.m. in the pre-opening session, which instruction can the broker enter?
column4: A cancellation of an earlier bid
column5: A reduction in an existing order's size
column6: An increase in the price of a resting bid
column7: The no-cancellation period permits new orders within its rules. Amendments and cancellations are unavailable.

column2: No final indicative equilibrium price can be established during pre-opening. How will the system match that stock?
column4: Match at the previous closing price
column5: Match at the midpoint of the quotes
column6: Use the last reported manual trade
column7: A pre-opening match requires a final equilibrium price. The system does not substitute a reference price in this session.

column2: Which bid has execution priority at pre-opening when both bids qualify at the final equilibrium price?
column5: Whichever bid has the larger quantity
column6: Whichever broker has more orders pending
column7: Order type takes priority before price and time. An at-auction order ranks ahead of an at-auction limit order even if entered later.

column2: Five nominal price snapshots are HK$31.10, 31.20, 31.15, 31.10 and 31.25. What is the closing auction reference price?
column7: The reference price is the median of the five observations. Sorting them places HK$31.15 in the middle.

column2: A closing auction has a HK$48.00 reference, HK$47.80 bid and HK$48.60 ask. No final IEP forms. Where does it close?
column7: When the auction cannot establish a final indicative equilibrium price, the reference price becomes the closing price. Averaging the final quotes would give HK$48.20.

column2: A stock's volatility control mechanism triggers during continuous trading. What can a dealer do during the cooling-off period?
column3: Execute at prices within prescribed limits
column4: Trade it only at the last execution price
column5: Submit orders for a reopening auction
column6: Switch to a market-wide closing auction
column7: The stock can still trade within the specified limits during the five-minute period. The mechanism applies at instrument level.

column2: On a regular Hong Kong trading day in November 2026, when does after-hours trading in Hang Seng Index futures open?
column7: The July 2026 timetable starts the after-hours session for this contract at 5:00 p.m. Some other derivatives have different starting times.

column2: A CNS participant buys 7,000 shares and sells 4,500 of the same issue for the same settlement day and currency. What is due?
column7: Netting offsets delivery and receipt obligations in the same issue. The purchases exceed sales by 2,500 shares.

column2: HKSCC isolates an exchange trade for risk management. Between whom does the resulting settlement exposure lie?
column7: HKSCC facilitates isolated settlement without stepping between the participants as central counterparty. It acts as central counterparty on a CNS trade.

column2: A CCASS custodian transfers shares to its client's Investor Participant account. Which transaction accommodates these parties?
column7: An ISI links an Investor Participant with another, non-investor participant. An ordinary SI links two non-investor participants.

column2: A CCASS broker needs to transfer shares now and has enough stock. What can it enter between batch runs?
column7: A delivery instruction takes immediate effect when the delivering stock clearing account has enough securities.

column2: Participants choose real-time delivery versus payment for an SI. What releases the securities to the paying participant?
column3: Confirmation of cash settlement by HKICL
column4: Acceptance of the order by SEHK
column7: The real-time arrangement credits the securities on receipt of payment confirmation. Matching instructions and transferring money are separate events.

column2: Two custodians elect free-of-payment settlement for a CCASS securities transfer. How do they settle any money due?
column4: By a mandatory end-of-day CNS debit
column5: Through an HKSCC real-time payment release
column6: With a debit to the issuer's dividend account
column7: HKSCC transfers the shares free of payment under this election. Participants arrange any associated cash payment separately.

column2: One client buys HK$25,250 of dutiable Hong Kong stock. With no remission, what stamp duty applies to the buyer?
column7: The rate is 0.1% on the buyer's side, rounded up to a whole dollar. The unrounded amount is HK$25.25.

column2: A client's agreed secondary market commission is 0.12%, subject to a HK$60 minimum. What brokerage applies to a HK$40,000 trade?
column7: Secondary market brokerage is negotiable. The percentage produces HK$48, so the contractual minimum applies instead.

column2: An IPO application covers HK$15,000 of shares. What is the standard brokerage component alone?
column7: The standard IPO brokerage is 1% of application money. Levies and the trading fee are separate components.

column2: A retail client sells HK$200,000 of ordinary shares. How much is the SFC transaction levy on her side?
column7: The levy of 0.0027% applies to the consideration on each side. Multiplying HK$200,000 by 0.000027 gives HK$5.40.

column2: At the normal SEHK trading fee rate, what exchange fee does a buyer pay on HK$80,000 of shares?
column7: The exchange charges 0.00565% per side. The SFC and AFRC levy rates are separate from this fee.

column2: A dealing desk receives an agency instruction and generates a house order. When should it time stamp the records?
column5: On matching for the house order only
column6: At client confirmation for the agency order
column7: Paragraph 3.9 covers agency orders and internally generated transactions. Their instruction details must be recorded and time stamped immediately.

column2: Under the SFC Code, what is the minimum retention period for recordings of client telephone order instructions?
column7: The Code sets a six-month minimum for the telephone recording itself. Other record types can have different requirements.

column2: Internal audit examines a broker's settlements department. Where should audit findings have a direct reporting route?
column3: Senior management or the audit committee
column6: The head of the dealing desk
column7: The SFC calls for an objective review function independent of operations where practicable. Direct access lets it report findings outside the unit examined.

column2: A dealer mistakenly buys 3,000 excess shares. Where should the broker book that position pending correction?
column7: The dealing error goes to the designated error or suspense account with a record of what happened. The position should be corrected or closed promptly.

column2: Which identifier normally accompanies a consenting retail client's securities order under Hong Kong's investor identification regime?
column7: The broker assigns a BCAN to the client and tags it to the order. The broker's own identifiers cannot distinguish one client from another.

column2: Where does an intermediary submit the mapping between a client's identification details and BCAN under HKIDR?
column7: The mapping in SEHK's repository connects the code on an order with client identity data. It has a different purpose from settlement and shareholder records.

column2: An individual withholds express consent under HKIDR. Which instruction can her broker still execute for her on SEHK?
column3: Sale of shares she already holds
column4: Purchase of shares she already holds
column6: Sale to open a new short position
column7: The restricted route allows disposal of existing holdings. It does not allow a new purchase or a sale opening a fresh position.

column2: A broker receives a reportable physical share certificate deposit from a client. Where does the OTC transaction report go?
column7: The OTC reporting regime directs information about reportable deposits and withdrawals to the SFC. The exchange repository receives different information under HKIDR.

column2: A complaint reveals the same fee error affected silent clients. Under the SFC Code, how far should the investigation extend?
column3: To other accounts exposed to the error
column4: To accounts that have requested mediation
column5: To complaints received in that month
column6: To clients covered by the same adviser only
column7: A broader problem identified in one complaint requires investigation and remedy for other affected clients, even if they have not complained.

column2: A client has HK$40,000 credit capacity left and submits an online order requiring HK$55,000. Which control addresses the excess before routing?
column7: Online trading controls should prevent orders that would exceed the relevant account threshold. Reconciliations and conduct surveillance address different risks.

column2: Which ongoing review checks completed market activity for possible manipulation?
column3: Post-trade surveillance of orders and transactions
column6: Periodic tests of peak message capacity
column7: Post-trade monitoring looks for potentially manipulative or abusive trading. It complements the checks made before an order can enter the market.

column2: How should a broker establish whether its online platform can handle a foreseeable surge in volume?
column3: Simulate peak conditions and record system behaviour
column4: Reconcile completed trades to contract notes
column5: Check that client credit limits were approved
column6: Verify that price feeds carry time stamps
column7: The SFC expects regular stress tests under simulated conditions. The broker should document the results and actions taken.

column2: An outage makes the broker's online order service unavailable. Which arrangement belongs in its client contingency plan?
column3: A backup route for placing instructions
column4: A review of dormant account balances
column5: A new limit for overnight market exposure
column6: A second source for closing valuations
column7: A written plan should provide a backup facility or alternative means of execution. Clients need to know how to submit instructions during disruption.
